Title: Diagnosis of test `testDoubleMetaphoneAlternate`
Details:
The failing test method `testDoubleMetaphoneAlternate` in `org.apache.commons.codec.language.DoubleMetaphone2Test` relies on a test data array `TEST_DATA` that provides inputs and expected outputs for the doubleMetaphone algorithm with the alternate flag set to true.

The failure happens because the actual output from the method `doubleMetaphone.doubleMetaphone(value, true)` does not match the expected alternate phonetic code for some inputs in the `TEST_DATA`.

Looking at the implementation of `DoubleMetaphone.doubleMetaphone(String value, boolean alternate)`, the method processes the input string into a phonetic code result object `DoubleMetaphoneResult`. It iterates over characters, appending phonetic codes depending on various rules until the code is complete. Finally, it returns either the primary or alternate code based on the `alternate` flag.

The `DoubleMetaphoneResult` methods `getPrimary()` and `getAlternate()` simply return the accumulated phonetic primary and alternate codes as strings.

Given that the test fails on the alternate phonetic code, the fault likely stems from the logic that appends alternate phonetic characters during the processing of the input string inside the various `handleX` methods or in how the alternate code is constructed within `DoubleMetaphoneResult`. It could also involve incorrect handling of specific letters or letter sequences that should produce a different alternate phonetic representation.

Hence, the root cause of the test failure is a discrepancy or bug in how alternate phonetic codes are generated or appended by the `DoubleMetaphone` class's internal logic when processing the input string.

Next we can review the `handleC` method or other handle methods to confirm if alternate codes are appended correctly or check `DoubleMetaphoneResult` candidate logic for handling alternate appends.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
